subject: Quick follow-up: unfiltered thoughts on Redwood's inference fit?
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@orchidai.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick follow-up: unfiltered thoughts on Redwood's inference fit?

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the candid conversation. I promised to send a short, no-friction recap so you can share this internally if helpful. Two quick things up front:

- TL;DR: We think Redwood could reduce per-request token cost by ~30% for your ML inference workload (50–200k inference/min peak) while keeping p95 latency under 200ms with a pilot using our dedciated capacity + KV-cache strategy.
- Primary constraints you called out: procurement timeline (Q1 budget), SOC2 evidence, and burst traffic during batch releases.

Call highlights (short):
- Current stack: in-house Triton endpoints + bespoke autoscaler — you have predictable daily batch spikes and unpredictable user-facing bursts.
- What matters: p95 latency at peak, cost per 1M tokens for embeddings & generation, and audit logs for data retention.
- Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot on a subset of models (1 generation model + 1 embedding model), Redwood Dedicated with a low-risk canary rollout and a pre-seeded KV cache.

Next-step ask: would you prefer (A) a 15-min technical sync to scope the pilot (I can bring our solutions engineer), or (B) a short draft SOW and anticipated pricing for you to circulate? If helpful I attached a one-page recap.

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood-PostCall-Recap.pdf (PDF)]

If no answer this week, I’ll do a quick check-in next week. Really interested in your unfiltered take — what feels like the biggest risk from your perspective?

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hey Nikhil / Marissa —

Thanks for the follow-ups and for the clear recap. Apologies for the delay — we’ve been buried with a release. A few candid notes from our side:

- Unfiltered risk: procurement + our security review cadence. We have a Q1 capital plan and need vendor paperwork in hand by end of Dec to be evaluated for the Q1 commit.
- Tech fit: sounds promising on paper — the latency numbers you mentioned are in the right band for our front-end experience.
- Pilot ask: we’d prefer a small, time-boxed POC that exercises peak bursts and a KV-cache scenario.

Raj (cc’d) will help with the security questionnaire — he prefers to see the SOC2 evidence and data retention policy before committing to a call. We can do the 20-minute sync on Tue 11/23 at 10:00am PT. Please send a calendar invite with the proposed agenda (20 min: 10 min engineering scope, 10 min security/evidence ask).

If you can also drop a one-page SOW and a short list of expected entitlements for the POC (compute envelope, expected token volume, estimation of run-hours), that will help speed internal sign-off.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Product, Orchid AI
